title.en: Reader Q&A: Rafael Behr answers your questions – live
title.zh: 读者问答：拉斐尔·贝尔在线回答您的问题

summary.en: The Guardian columnist Rafael Behr is engaging with readers in a live Q&A session, addressing questions about British politics, including the decade since Brexit, and current political figures like Burnham and Starmer.
summary.zh: 《卫报》专栏作家拉斐尔·贝尔正在与读者进行在线问答，回答有关英国政治的问题，包括脱欧十年来的情况，以及伯纳姆和斯塔默等当前政治人物。

body.en: It’s 10 years since Brexit – and it’s also another one of those weeks in British politics … Guardian columnist Rafael Behr is online now answering your questions about Burnham, Starmer, Brexit and more. Sign up here to join the discussion and post your questions MrGluben asks: Is the compromise of rejoining the single market via membership of the EFTA (and by extension the EEA), the so-called Norway option, still a possibility? Raf: Absolutely, at least from a technical point of view. And the Lib Dems recently made this their policy precisely in the hope of putting pressure on a new (Burnham, presumably) government to move in that direction. In some respects the EEA/EFTA idea is easier because it’s an off-the shelf model and would give Brussels a clearer sense of the destination the UK has in mind, making the negotiations easier to structure. The problems are, of course, political. The big one is freedom of movement, which is a non-negotiable part of SM membership. When I asked Ed Davey’s office about this, I was told he thinks it’s a winnable argument : that the British public are so down on Brexit, so aware that it has gone wrong, and mindful that leaving th EU hardly dealt the immigration issue anyway, that freedom of movement could be sold as a reciprocal benefit and that the merits of a much closer relationship with our continental neighbours would facilitate better cooperation on other migration issues, chiefly the small boat crossings. There is some polling evidence to support that optimistic view. The European Council for Foreign Relations has a new poll out that suggests freedom of movement, if advertised as part of a package of general trade and economic integration, is acceptable to a majority of people by a surprising margin . There is another problem with EEA/Norway etc, which is the old “soft Brexit” issue of rule-taking. As members of the single market but not full members of the EU, the UK would end up aligning with regulations over which it has very little say or agency. This is one of the bitterest ironies of Brexit. The eurosceptic myth of Brussels “dictating” laws to parliament never took account of the power that British ministers had on the European council, often with veto powers. “Europe” was not something “they” did to “us” but something we did to and for ourselves. But once we left, the threat of taking dictation became a self-fulfilling prophecy. Our interests demand closeness to the single market but proximity without a voice really is a loss of sovereignty. Maybe worth it, but not great. That’s the logic that dragged us towards ever harder iterations of Brexit, leading to the deal we now have, which turns out to be disastrous. body.zh: 英国脱欧已经过去 10 年了，这也是英国政治的又一个星期……卫报专栏作家拉斐尔·贝尔现在在线回答您有关伯纳姆、斯塔默、英国脱欧等问题。在此注册加入讨论并提出您的问题，MrGluben 提出的问题：通过加入欧洲自由贸易联盟（以及扩展的欧洲经济区）重新加入单一市场（即所谓的挪威选项）的妥协方案是否仍然可行？ Raf：当然，至少从技术角度来看是这样。自由民主党最近将此作为他们的政策，正是希望向新政府（大概是伯纳姆）施加压力，迫使其朝这个方向前进。在某些方面，欧洲经济区/欧洲自由贸易联盟的想法更容易，因为它是一个现成的模型，可以让布鲁塞尔更清楚地了解英国心目中的目的地，从而使谈判更容易安排。当然，这些问题是政治性的。最重要的是行动自由，这是 SM 会员身份不可协商的一部分。当我向埃德·戴维的办公室询问此事时，我被告知他认为这是一个可以获胜的论点：英国公众对英国退欧如此不满，如此意识到它出了问题，并且意识到离开欧盟无论如何都很难解决移民问题，迁徙自由可以作为互惠利益出售，而且与我们大陆邻国建立更密切关系的好处将有助于在其他移民问题上更好地合作，主要是在小船过境问题上。有一些民意调查证据支持这种乐观观点。欧洲外交关系委员会的一项新民意调查显示，如果将行动自由作为一般贸易和经济一体化一揽子计划的一部分进行宣传，那么大多数人会以惊人的比例接受行动自由。欧洲经济区/挪威等国家还存在另一个问题，即古老的“软脱欧”规则接受问题。作为单一市场成员但不是欧盟正式成员，英国最终将遵守其几乎没有发言权或代理权的法规。这是英国脱欧最苦涩的讽刺之一。布鲁塞尔向议会“制定”法律的欧洲怀疑论神话从未考虑到英国部长们在欧洲理事会中拥有的权力，通常具有否决权。 “欧洲”不是“他们”对“我们”所做的事情，而是我们对自己所做的事情。但一旦我们离开，听写的威胁就变成了一个自我实现的预言。我们的利益要求接近单一市场，但接近却没有发言权实际上就是主权的丧失。也许值得，但不是很好。这就是拖累我们走向更加艰难的脱欧迭代的逻辑，导致了我们现在达成的协议，结果证明这是灾难性的。拉夫：我认为如果没有……就很难制定像重新加入欧盟这样重要的事情。

On Monday night, Jon Stewart addressed Donald Trump turning DC’s reflecting pool “Mountain Dew green”, his blundered Iran peace deal and wasting US taxpayer money.

On the Daily Show, Stewart joked that the US administration has been trying to find a solution to a “problematic waterway in a dangerous part of the world”. The host was referencing the Lincoln Memorial reflecting pool, which has turned green from algae growth after bungled paint job.

“This is really fucking green,” Stewart said. “Did they replace the water with Mountain Dew?”

The host then made a link between the pool’s color and the name of the company hired to fix the problem: Greenwater Services.

“Quite perplexing”, he deadpanned, stroking his chin. “How did it get so green?”

“I kid, of course, it’s not about the name,” Stewart said, before adding sarcastically: “I’m sure Greenwater Services is a very reputable company that fairly won the reflecting pool contract because of their expertise and track record.” (Greenwater Services is owned by the Republican donor, John J Cafaro.)

“Does Trump do business with anyone normal?” Stewart questioned. “Even the pool guy looks like an extra from Guys and Dolls.”

Cafaro was convicted of bribing a member of Congress in 2001. “The pool guy bribed the congressman and now he gets the pool contract?” asked the host. “That tracks.” He went on to impersonate a gangster, saying: “What do I do? Let’s just say I’m in the chlorine management business.”

Stewart then reacted to a viral video of JD Vance being snubbed by Qatari leaders while in Switzerland for peace talks.

“Well, that is awkward,” said Stewart, after playing footage of the vice-president looking awkward as world leaders exchanged hugs and greetings. “JD Vance really answers the question, ‘What if a middle school dance were a person?’”

“Things just went from bad to wallflower with Vance getting more and more exasperated, as the mean girls just couldn’t see that he has a lot to offer too,” Stewart added.

“So basically, JD Vance is just there to pick up the white flag, get it signed, hand out a couple of orange slices, call it a game,” joked Stewart.

title.en: US top court says Rastafarian man cannot sue prison guards who cut his dreadlocks
title.zh: 美国最高法院称拉斯特法里男子不能起诉剪掉他辫子的狱警

summary.en: The Rastafarian man argued his religious rights were violated after prison officials focibly shaved off his hair.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The US Supreme Court has ruled that a former Louisiana inmate cannot sue prison officials who forcibly shaved his dreadlocks in violation of his Rastafarian faith.

In a 6-3 ruling, the top court said the prisoner, Damon Landor, was not entitled to monetary damages under a federal religious freedom law as it did not apply to individual officials.

The justices said state employees did not consent to face lawsuits in their personal capacities when Congress passed the the Religious Land Use and Institutionalized Persons Act (RLUIPA) in 2000.

The ruling marks a departure from a series of recent Supreme Court decisions, in which the justices have generally sided with religious-liberty claims.

In 2020, when Landor was serving time for a drug-related charge, officers handcuffed him to a chair and shaved his head after he argued it would violate his religious rights as a Rastafarian.

In a statement to USA Today, Landor said his dreadlocks are "a part of me and part of who I am".

Growing uncut, uncombed hair into dreadlocks is a symbol of devotion and spiritual growth for Rastafarians.

In the opinion on Tuesday, Conservative justices ruled against Landor, while three liberal justices dissented.

Justice Neil Gorsuch wrote that RLUPIA, which applies to local prisons that receive federal funding, does not allow for legal challenges against individual officials.

"Under the Spending Clause, Congress lacks regulatory authority to impose liability on them directly and must depend instead on consent," Gorsuch wrote.

In her dissent, liberal Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson said the goal of RLUIPA was to "ensure that state and local prisons respect prisoners' right to religious exercise".
body.zh: 美国最高法院裁定，一名前路易斯安那州囚犯不能起诉监狱官员，因为监狱官员违反了他的拉斯塔法里信仰，强行剃掉了他的辫子。 最高法院以 6 比 3 的裁决表示，根据联邦宗教自由法，囚犯达蒙·兰多 (Damon Landor) 无权获得金钱赔偿，因为该法不适用于个别官员。 法官们表示，当国会于 2000 年通过《宗教土地使用和收容人员法案》(RLUIPA) 时，国家雇员并不同意以个人身份面对诉讼。 这项裁决标志着最高法院最近做出的一系列裁决的背离，在这些裁决中，法官们普遍支持宗教自由主张。 2020 年，当兰多因与毒品有关的指控而服刑时，警察将他铐在椅子上，并剃光了他的头发，因为他认为这会侵犯他作为拉斯特法里教徒的宗教权利。 兰多在《今日美国》的一份声明中表示，他的辫子是“我的一部分，也是我的一部分”。 对于拉斯塔法里教徒来说，将未修剪、未梳理的头发留成辫子是奉献和精神成长的象征。 在周二的意见中，保守党法官做出了对兰多不利的裁决，而三名自由派法官则表示反对。 尼尔·戈萨奇法官写道，RLUPIA 适用于接受联邦资助的当地监狱，不允许对个别官员提出法律质疑。 戈萨奇写道：“根据支出条款，国会缺乏监管机构直接对他们施加责任，而必须依赖于他们的同意。” 自由派法官 Ketanji Brown Jackson 在她的异议中表示，RLUIPA 的目标是“确保州和地方监狱尊重囚犯进行宗教活动的权利”。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to justice, dignity, and accountability. Micah 6:8 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with justice tempered by mercy, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到公义、尊严与问责。Micah 6:8提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以带着怜悯的公义来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: What does Yahweh require of you? To act justly and to love mercy and to walk humbly with your God.
verse.textZh: 雅伟向你所要的是什么呢？只要你行公义，好怜悯，存谦卑的心，与你的神同行。

summary.en: Before being imprisoned for 20 years, Jimmy Lai founded Hong Kong's largest pro-democracy newspaper. His son said the award shows that those who fight for the freedom of others "are never alone."

body.en:
Before being imprisoned for 20 years, Jimmy Lai founded Hong Kong's largest pro-democracy newspaper. His son said the award shows that those who fight for the freedom of others "are never alone."

Arriving in Hong Kong as a penniless 12-year-old stowaway from southern China, Jimmy Lai sought only freedom and a future. At the time, Lai could never have imagined how his life would become forever intertwined with this former British colony.

"I'll sink with the ship, because this place gives me everything," said Lai in an interview about Hong Kong with DW a few months before he was taken into custody in December 2020. He was one of the first high-profile figures to be targeted under a "national security law" imposed on Hong Kong by Beijing following a crackdown on pro-democracy protests.

Beijing had said the law would restore Hong Kong "from chaos to order" after demonstrations in 2019 opposing an extradition bill morphed into massive protests against Beijing encroaching on Hong Kong's civil liberties .

Since then, the pro-democracy media mogul has spent more than 2,000 days in solitary confinement in Hong Kong's maximum-security Stanley Prison.

Lai's years-long trial ended this February, when the 78-year-old was sentenced to 20 years in prison for "colluding with foreign forces." While he had pleaded not guilty to all charges, his legal team said he will not appeal.

The sentence is the heaviest punishment handed down so far under the national security law, and Lai's trial has symbolized for many people the severe erosion of press freedom in Hong Kong as part of Beijing's broader strategy to silence critical voices.

In recognition of his defense of press freedom and freedom of speech, DW honored Jimmy Lai with this year's Freedom of Speech Award  at the annual Global Media Forum in Bonn, Germany, on Tuesday.

"While we have spoken freely in the defence of independent media, Jimmy, who founded an independent media company because he believed in the rights of the Hong Kong people to receive information, is locked away for those beliefs," Jodie Ginsberg, CEO of the Committee to Protect Journalists, said in a speech honoring Lai.

"The attacks on Apple Daily and its counterparts in Hong Kong presaged the far greater attacks on civil liberties in the years that followed. Jimmy Lai saw this and spoke out. We can honor him today not only by fighting for his freedom, but by defending the freedoms for which he was jailed."

Since 2015, the DW Freedom of Speech Award has honored journalists and human rights defenders as a way to call attention to restrictions on press freedom and concerning human rights situations around the world.

title.en: Dozens of ships head through Strait of Hormuz after US-Iran deal
title.zh: 美国与伊朗达成协议后，数十艘船只通过霍尔木兹海峡

summary.en: Traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has significantly increased, with 42 ships passing through on a single Saturday, following a recent deal between the United States and Iran aimed at ending the war.
summary.zh: 在美国和伊朗签署了一项旨在结束战争的协议后，霍尔木兹海峡的交通量显著增加，仅周六一天就有42艘船只通过。

body.en:
At least 172 vessels have crossed through the Strait of Hormuz since the US and Iran signed a deal aimed at ending the war, including 42 ships on Saturday alone, according to new data from maritime intelligence firm Kpler.

The number of vessels making the transit from 18 June, the day after the deal was signed, is still well below the pre-conflict average of some 138 crossings each day.

Ship-tracking data analysed by BBC Verify shows more than 200 tankers appear to be waiting inside the strait on Tuesday, with at least 10 ships moving west into the Gulf so far.

The price of a barrel of Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, has dropped to its lowest level since the war began.

Many of the tankers that have transited the strait in recent days have been linked with Iran following the lifting of the US naval blockade as part of the deal.

At least 30 tankers have departed from the Gulf laden with Iranian oil and petrochemicals since the deal was agreed, according to Jemima Shelley, a senior research analyst at the United Against Nuclear Iran campaign and monitoring group.

The US Treasury has also eased decades-old sanctions by issuing a license to allow the sale of Iranian crude oil, petrochemicals and other oil products until 21 August.

On Monday at least five tankers previously sanctioned by the US for links with Iran moved through the strait, ship tracking data shows, carrying up to four million barrels of oil.

"That said, there has been an increase in 'normal' trade too," said Martin Kelly of crisis management firm EOS Risk Group.

Four liquefied natural gas tankers were seen on ship-tracking platforms heading through the strait to Qatar's Ras Laffan port on Monday and at least three tankers and three cargo vessels sailed out of the Gulf on Tuesday.

All of these transits were made along the Iranian-approved northern route through Iranian waters, rather than the US-recommended southern route close to the coast of Oman.

And, according to ship-tracking data, more than 250 tankers and 440 cargo ships are still inside the Gulf, based on their last reported positions. More than 80% of the tankers are stationary or at anchor and about one in six appears to be carrying cargo.

Despite the US and its Gulf allies repeatedly rejecting Iranian attempts to exert control over the strait during the conflict, the deal signed last week committed Iran to using its "best efforts for the safe passage of commercial vessels with no charge for 60 days".

The agreement also said Iran will work with Oman to "define the future administration and maritime services" of the strait.

title.en: India: What’s driving the intense pressure on students?
title.zh: 印度：是什么给学生带来了巨大的压力？

summary.en: The reported deaths of aspiring medical students in India have exposed the immense pressures of the country's high-stakes examination system and a worsening mental-health crisis.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The reported deaths of aspiring medical students in India have exposed the immense pressures of the country's high-stakes examination system and a worsening mental-health crisis.

When 18-year-old Nelima Patel sat down to retake the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) medical entrance examination in the western Indian city of Ahmedabad on Sunday, she felt completely drained before the exam had even begun.  

The original test in early May was canceled over suspicions that the questions had been leaked. Patel had to prepare all over again, navigating uncertainty, exhaustion and anxiety.

"It was mentally exhausting, but I had to keep my wits about me while writing," Patel told DW. "There was just too much preparation that went into it."

"Just a few days earlier, another student I knew died by suicide. It was all upsetting," she said.

Across the country, thousands of students found themselves in a similar position.

What was supposed to be the culmination of years of preparation suddenly morphed into just another period of insecurity following the cancellation of the original exam.

This weekend, more than 2 million medical aspirants retook the exam under multi-layered security across thousands of centers, featuring strict surveillance measures like facial authentication, biometric checks and thousands of signal jammers.

India offers roughly 130,000 medical undergraduate seats — distributed across more than 800 medical colleges nationwide — for the 2.27 million students who took the NEET medical entrance exam this year.

That means fewer than one in 17 candidates can secure a place in a medical college.

"It is unfair to put children through such a torturous process," said Rukmini Madhavan, whose son, Mahesh, also took the examination again.

"If they don't make the cut-off, the problems are compounded and can have a mental toll," she said.

The emotional strain surrounding NEET has once again exposed a larger and more troubling reality of India's growing crisis of student distress.

Worryingly, 12 NEET aspirants have reportedly died by suicide in the days since the examination controversy erupted.

Some left behind notes detailing the immense strain they were under, while others had expressed anxiety about enduring another round of preparation and testing.

Their deaths have sparked fresh questions about an education system in which a handful of examinations often determine access to universities, careers and, many believe, a family's future.

Many of these students come from low-income or rural backgrounds where parents take out massive private loans, sell land, or drain savings to fund years of expensive coaching institute fees.

body.zh: 据报道，印度有抱负的医学生死亡事件暴露了该国高风险考试制度的巨大压力和日益恶化的心理健康危机。 周日，当 18 岁的内利玛·帕特尔 (Nelima Patel) 在印度西部城市艾哈迈达巴德重新参加国家资格暨入学考试 (NEET) 医学入学考试时，考试还没开始，她就感到筋疲力尽。 原本五月初的考试因怀疑试题泄露而被取消。 帕特尔必须重新做好准备，应对不确定性、疲惫和焦虑。 帕特尔告诉德国之声：“这让我精神疲惫，但我在写作时必须保持头脑清醒。” “这里面的准备工作太多了。” “就在几天前，我认识的另一名学生自杀身亡。这令人心烦意乱，”她说。 全国各地有成千上万的学生发现自己处于类似的境地。 本来应该是多年准备的高潮突然变成了原考试取消后的另一个不安全时期。 本周末，超过 200 万有志于医学的考生在数千个中心的多层安全保护下重新参加了考试，其中包括面部身份验证、生物识别检查和数千个信号干扰器等严格的监控措施。 印度为今年参加 NEET 医学入学考试的 227 万名学生提供了大约 13 万个医学本科席位，分布在全国 800 多所医学院。 这意味着只有不到十分之一的候选人能够进入医学院。 鲁克米尼·马达万 (Rukmini Madhavan) 说：“让孩子们经历如此痛苦的过程是不公平的。”他的儿子马赫什 (Mahesh) 也再次参加了考试。 “如果他们没有达到要求，问题就会变得更加复杂，并可能造成精神损失，”她说。 围绕尼特族的情绪压力再次暴露了印度日益严重的学生困境危机这一更大、更令人不安的现实。 令人担忧的是，据报道，自考试争议爆发以来，已有 12 名 NEET 考生自杀身亡。 一些人留下了笔记，详细描述了他们所承受的巨大压力，而另一些人则表达了对承受另一轮准备和测试的焦虑。 他们的去世引发了人们对教育体系的新质疑，在教育体系中，少数考试往往决定着大学的入学机会、职业生涯，以及许多人认为的家庭的未来。 这些学生中有许多来自低收入或农村背景，他们的父母通过大量私人贷款、出售土地或耗尽积蓄来支付多年来昂贵的教练机构费用。 据统计，2024 年该国有 14,488 名学生自杀。

summary.en: Forty people have drowned in heatwave-related deaths in France since last Thursday, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu says.
summary.zh: 法国总理塞巴斯蒂安·勒科尔努表示，自上周四以来，法国已有40人因热浪相关原因溺水身亡。

body.en:
Forty people have drowned in heatwave-related deaths in France since last Thursday, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu has said, as temperatures hit record levels in several major cities and the heatwave reaches a peak in several European countries.

"It's not something to be taken lightly, going swimming in unsupervised areas during a heatwave," Sports and Youth Minister Marina Ferrari told French radio.

France, along with Spain and Italy, has been hardest hit by the heatwave so far.

France saw its hottest June day on record on Monday and its hottest ever night on Monday night, with a minimum average of 21.6C according to Météo France, and with well over half the country on red alert.

Meanwhile, in Spain temperatures are set to peak above 40C in some areas, with red alerts in Andalusia in the south, and Cantabria and the Basque Country in the north, on the third day of a national heatwave.

Spain is more exposed to the effects of climate change than almost any other European country. State weather service Aemet says June heatwaves are becoming increasingly common, with 10 recorded in mainland Spain between 2000 and 2025, and just two in the previous 25 years.

And in Italy, a red heatwave alert has been declared in 15 cities, including Rome, Milan, Florence, Turin and Venice. The alert signals conditions that can pose health risks even to healthy adults, not just the elderly or chronically ill.

France's sports minister said too many people were trying to cool off in rivers and canals without necessarily taking the risks into account.

Among the fatalities was a 13-year-old girl who had gone for a dip with her family in the River Seine at Fontaine-La Port on Sunday evening, although she did not know how to swim.

Meanwhile, a young professional footballer was in critical condition in hospital after being pulled out of the River Rhône in a park near Lyon. Emergency services were called to the area to rescue four young men who had got into difficulty in an area of the river where swimming is banned.

Two other deaths on Monday were also blamed on the extreme heat in France, after children aged two and four were found in their family car in a car park in the southern city of Carpentras.

Several people have also drowned in Germany as temperatures are expected to climb as high as 40C in the west and south-west by the end of the week.

The German Lifesaving Association (DLRG) said there were six fatal swimming incidents between Friday and Sunday with men in particular were overestimating their abilities in the water. Three bodies were found in the Rhine near the southwestern town of Biblis, days after three men aged 23, 27 and 50 were reported missing in two different areas of the river.

body.zh: 法国总理塞巴斯蒂安·勒科尔努表示，自上周四以来，法国已有 40 人因热浪而溺水身亡，几个主要城市的气温达到创纪录水平，几个欧洲国家的热浪达到了顶峰。 体育和青年部长玛丽娜·法拉利对法国电台表示：“热浪期间在无人监管的地方游泳并不是一件可以掉以轻心的事情。” 迄今为止，法国、西班牙和意大利是受热浪打击最严重的国家。 法国周一迎来了有记录以来最热的六月一天，周一晚上也创下了有史以来最热的夜晚，根据法国气象局的数据，最低平均气温为 21.6 摄氏度，超过一半的国家处于红色警戒状态。 与此同时，西班牙部分地区气温将达到40摄氏度以上，全国热浪进入第三天，南部安达卢西亚、北部坎塔布里亚和巴斯克地区将出现红色警报。 西班牙比几乎所有其他欧洲国家都更容易受到气候变化的影响。国家气象局 Aemet 表示，6 月的热浪变得越来越普遍，2000 年至 2025 年间，西班牙大陆记录了 10 次热浪，而在过去 25 年中仅记录了 2 次。 在意大利，罗马、米兰、佛罗伦萨、都灵和威尼斯等 15 个城市已发布热浪红色警报。该警报发出的信号表明，这些情况甚至可能对健康成年人构成健康风险，而不仅仅是老年人或慢性病患者。 法国体育部长表示，太多人试图在河流和运河中降温，而没有考虑到风险。 死亡人数中包括一名 13 岁女孩，她周日晚上与家人在方丹拉港的塞纳河里游泳，尽管她不会游泳。 与此同时，一名年轻的职业足球运动员被从里昂附近的一个公园的罗纳河中救出，目前情况危急，正在医院接受治疗。紧急服务人员被呼叫到该地区营救四名在禁止游泳的河流区域陷入困境的年轻人。 周一，法国南部城市卡庞特拉的一个停车场内，有人发现两岁和四岁的儿童在自家车里，导致另外两人死亡，也被归咎于法国的酷热天气。 德国也有多人溺水身亡，预计到本周末，西部和西南部气温将升至 40 摄氏度。 德国救生协会（DLRG）表示，周五至周日期间发生了六起致命游泳事件，尤其是男性高估了自己在水中的能力。几天前，三名年龄分别为 23 岁、27 岁和 50 岁的男子据报在莱茵河的两个不同地区失踪，在西南小镇比布利斯附近的莱茵河中发现了三具尸体。 西班牙 Aemet 气象服务机构称气温可能高达 44 摄氏度...

reflection.en: The tragic loss of forty lives due to heatwave-related drownings reminds us of the profound vulnerability of humanity and the natural world. Yahweh's word speaks of creation itself groaning under the weight of brokenness, a lament echoed in every human tragedy. In these moments, we are called to compassion and to seek ways to alleviate suffering in a world...
reflection.zh: 法国因热浪相关溺水事件导致四十人丧生的悲剧，提醒我们人类和自然世界深刻的脆弱性。雅伟的话语提到受造界本身在破碎的重压下呻吟，这在每一个人间悲剧中都有所体现。在这些时刻，我们被呼召去怜悯，并寻求方法来减轻这个深受环境挑战影响的世界的苦难。

verse.textEn: We know that the whole creation has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth right up to the present time.
verse.textZh: 我们知道，一切受造之物一同叹息、劳苦，直到如今。

title.en: From cool-down spots to chalk on windows - how Europeans are coping with the heat
title.zh: 从降温点到窗户上的粉笔——欧洲人如何应对炎热天气

summary.en: People across the continent are taking measures to cope with the searing temperatures gripping Europe.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Europe is in the throes of a scorching heatwave, with temperature records expected to tumble in the coming days.

We asked our reporters across the continent how people are dealing with the searing temperatures where they are.

Amsterdam is rolling out a network of "cool‑down" spots across the city, offering residents a place to escape the worst of the heat.

These spaces - in libraries, city farms, theatres, churches, community centres and even supermarkets - provide seating, drinking water and toilets, and many are open to pets as well.

In the pilot phase, most of the 12 cool‑down spots will be concentrated in Nieuw‑West, the district that city modelling identified as facing the greatest heat risk.

Officials weighed up how much shade is available, how many vulnerable residents such as young children and older people live there, and how quickly homes heat up.

Schools are also adapting. Many are moving to "tropical" timetables in the coming days, with shorter school days or fewer lessons, more breaks, extra drinks and increased ventilation.

Each school decides its own measures as there is no legal maximum classroom temperature.

The guiding principle is that pupils and teachers must be able to work in conditions that are safe and healthy.

The town hall of the 10th arrondissement of Paris is offering free cinema tickets to help people get out of the heat.

To qualify you have to be under 25 or over 65, and the offer is for afternoon sessions only.

Cinemas, libraries and museums have been identified as places where people should be encouraged to go to escape the punishing temperatures.

Some towns, such as Lyon, have temporarily suspended charging in municipal museums.

According to French newspapers, there has been a run on a chalky product called Blanc de Meudon, or Meudon Whiting, in DIY shops.

The powder is mixed with water and then painted on windows, thus diminishing the power of the sun's rays and in theory bringing down the inside temperature. It does actually seem to work.

The north-eastern Spanish region of Aragón is seeing some of the highest temperatures of the heatwave, and in the cities of Zaragoza and Huesca local authorities have responded by reducing the price of entry for public swimming pools.

The northern city of Logroño, which is expecting temperatures of up to 40C on Tuesday, has made entrance to swimming pools free for the duration of the heatwave and authorities there have announced that ornamental water fountains will be turned on until 23:00 at night.

People can also cool off under water sprinklers which have been switched on in several areas of the city.

body.zh: 欧洲正处于酷热热浪的痛苦之中，预计未来几天气温将刷新纪录。 我们询问了整个非洲大陆的记者，人们如何应对当地的酷热天气。 阿姆斯特丹正在全市推出“降温”点网络，为居民提供躲避酷暑的场所。 这些空间——图书馆、城市农场、剧院、教堂、社区中心甚至超市——提供座位、饮用水和厕所，而且许多空间还对宠物开放。 在试点阶段，12 个降温点中的大部分将集中在 Nieuw-West，该地区被城市模型确定为面临最大的高温风险。 官员们权衡了有多少阴凉处、有多少弱势居民（例如幼儿和老年人）居住在那里，以及房屋升温的速度。 学校也在适应。未来几天，许多学校将转向“热带”时间表，缩短上课时间或减少课程，增加休息时间，提供额外饮料并加强通风。 由于没有法定的最高教室温度，每所学校都会决定自己的措施。 指导原则是学生和教师必须能够在安全和健康的条件下工作。 巴黎第十区市政厅提供免费电影票，帮助人们避暑。 要获得资格，您的年龄必须在 25 岁以下或 65 岁以上，并且该优惠仅适用于下午课程。 电影院、图书馆和博物馆被认为是应该鼓励人们去躲避酷暑的地方。 里昂等一些城镇已暂时停止市博物馆收费。 据法国报纸报道，DIY 商店中出现了一种名为“Blanc de Meudon”或“Meudon Whiting”的白垩产品的抢购热潮。 将粉末与水混合，然后涂在窗户上，从而减弱太阳光线的强度，理论上可以降低室内温度。它看起来确实有效。 西班牙东北部的阿拉贡地区正经历热浪的最高气温，萨拉戈萨和韦斯卡等城市的地方当局已通过降低公共游泳池的入场费来应对。 北部城市洛格罗尼奥预计周二气温将高达 40 摄氏度，在热浪期间，游泳池免费开放，当地政府还宣布，装饰性喷泉将开放至夜间 23:00。 人们还可以在城市多个地区开启的喷水装置下乘凉。 由于火灾带来的风险，一些地方暂停了传统的篝火庆祝圣胡安节（施洗者约翰节）的活动。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to peace-making and restraint. Matthew 5:9 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with mercy, truth, and restraint, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.

verse.textEn: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
verse.textZh: 使人和睦的人有福了，因为他们必称为神的儿子。

title.en: Kenya Health Minister says halting US-backed Ebola quarantine center
title.zh: 肯尼亚卫生部长表示停止美国支持的埃博拉检疫中心

summary.en: Health Minister Aden Duale told a court he ordered an immediate stop to construction, after being held in contempt for ignoring previous court orders. The plans to set up the facility prompted protests and unrest.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.zh: 卫生部长亚丁·杜阿勒 (Aden Duale) 在法庭上表示，他因无视先前的法庭命令而被视为蔑视法庭，因此下令立即停止施工。建立该设施的计划引发了抗议和骚乱。 肯尼亚卫生部长亚丁·杜阿莱周二向肯尼亚法院保证，他已下令立即停止在空军基地建造美国支持的埃博拉检疫设施。 周一，杜阿勒因未能遵守先前暂停施工的命令，等待司法部门评估而被判藐视法庭。 位于中心城镇纳纽基的帐篷设施原本应该作为美国国民在刚果民主共和国疫情期间感染埃博拉病毒的治疗中心。 该项目于五月首次宣布，有时会引发暴力抗议，附近共有三人被杀。 在收到部长的保证后，法官帕特里夏·尼亚温迪·曼德 (Patricia Nyaundi Mande) 释放了杜阿勒 (Duale)，并没有进一步处罚，但警告他不要再继续不服从命令。 杜阿勒在周二的量刑听证会上表示：“我已指示立即完全停止任何有关莱基皮亚空军基地设施的预期建设、场地准备或相关活动，等待实质性请愿书的听证会和裁决，或直至法院发出进一步命令。” 该设施建于距首都内罗毕约 200 公里（125 英里）的拉基皮亚空军基地，设有约 50 个隔离床位。预计美国医务人员会处理好此事。 该计划引起了国内的强烈反对和抗议。肯尼亚从未记录过埃博拉病例，公众对将患者带到其领土上感到担忧，甚至直接将他们空运到安全的医疗机构。 人权组织也成功向法院请愿，称该设施是在未经协商的情况下秘密建造的。政府最初无视暂停施工等待检查的命令。 航班跟踪数据、卫星图像和不愿透露姓名的美国官员都指出，尽管法院发出了最初的命令，但现场仍在继续进行准备工作。 迄今为止，在本次疫情中感染埃博拉病毒的唯一美国公民是一名在刚果民主共和国东部疫情中心担任医疗传教士的医生，他已被飞往德国，在柏林的一家专业机构接受治疗。 肯尼亚不与刚果接壤，但位于乌干达东部，与刚果民主共和国东部伊图里省的震中接壤。 与此同时，世界卫生组织的一位高级官员在日内瓦举行的新闻发布会上表示……

reflection.en: This story draws attention to leadership, wisdom, and public responsibility. Proverbs 11:14 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with wisdom, integrity, and service, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.

title.en: Irish government to contribute £197m to cross-border rail services
title.zh: 爱尔兰政府将捐助1.97亿英镑用于跨境铁路服务

summary.en: The money will come from the last allocation from the Irish government's Shared Island Fund.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Irish government is to contribute €228m (£197m) towards improving rail services between Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland.

Some €193m (£166m) will go towards the Londonderry-Belfast-Dublin rail infrastructure investment and a further €35m (£30m) will be spent on continuing hourly trains from Dublin to Belfast, which will see the service continue until at least 2030.

The money will come from the last allocation from the Irish government's Shared Island Fund. , external

It is part of a scheme which aims to fund cross-border projects that benefit people in both the Republic and Northern Ireland.

The two governments will work together for a 15-20 minute transfer time between the Dublin-Belfast and Belfast-Derry lines to enhance connectivity between and the three cities.

Cabinet ministers on Tuesday in Dublin were told that total allocations under the fund are over €1bn (£862m) and approved plans for a further €377m (£325m) from the Shared Island Fund for 12 new projects to be delivered as part of the Initiative over 2027-2030.

The government will also contribute £3m towards cricket facilities at Stormont estate in Belfast.

The facilities are being redeveloped in the hopes of being one of the locations for co-hosting games in Northern Ireland as part of a joint hosting by Ireland and the UK of the Men's T20 Cricket World Cup in 2030.

Cricket Ireland and Northern Ireland Civil Service Sports Association are also contributing £1m (€1.15m) each towards expansion of the sports grounds.

The T20 World Cup will require multiple international-standard venues across Ireland and the UK.

It is likely to be the largest sporting event ever held on the island in terms of broadcast reach and overseas engagement, with the 2022 T20 World Cup having 3.95bn hours watched across all platforms.

There will also be a €40m(£34m) contribution towards a port development scheme which will enable expansion in capacity at ports across the island.

A further €30m (£26m) will be allocated for the third phase of the Ulster Canal restoration.

Phase 3, from Clonfad to Castle Saunderson, is the major blueway stage of the restoration project, and consists of 10km (6.2 miles) of new and refurbished navigable canal, linking Clones to the Erne System and the Shannon-Erne waterway.

A new 9km (5.5 miles) section Ulster Canal Greenway will be developed as part of the project, running from Clones to Gortnacarrow.

Lough Neagh will also receive a €33m (£28m) contribution from the Shared Island Fund for a new Lough Neagh Catchment Area Water Quality (LNWQ) programme.

The money comes after politicians discussed algae issues at Lough Neagh at North South Ministerial Council meetings.

title.en: Afghan Taliban clamp down on women, smartphones, protests
title.zh: 阿富汗塔利班镇压妇女、智能手机和抗议活动

summary.en: The Taliban are tightening the screws on women's clothing, shooting at protesters and ordering even their own officials to stop using smartphones. Behind the regime's omnipresent control, there are signs of deep anxiety.

title.en: Why Keir Starmer is stepping down — and what happens next
title.zh: 凯尔·斯塔默 (Keir Starmer) 为何辞职——以及接下来会发生什么

summary.en: The UK will now prepare for its seventh prime minister as Labour seeks a political reset following months of falling popularity.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
United Kingdom Prime Minister Keir Starmer has announced he will step down as leader of the Labour Party and leave office within weeks, ending a government that swept to power in a landslide election victory less than two years ago.

Starmer said he will remain in Downing Street as caretaker prime minister until Labour chooses a replacement, setting in motion another leadership transition in a country that has cycled through prime ministers at remarkable speed in the post-Brexit era.

The decision follows months of mounting political pressure , deteriorating public support and growing concern within Labour that the government had lost the confidence of voters.

Speaking outside Number 10 on Monday, an emotional Starmer said he had informed King Charles III of his intention to resign and would work to ensure an orderly transfer of power.

"Every decision I have taken has been about putting the country I love first," he said.

His departure makes him the sixth UK prime minister in a decade to announce an early exit.

Starmer entered office in July 2024 with one of Labour's strongest election victories in decades.

After 14 years of Conservative government, Labour promised political stability, economic repair and a reset of public trust.

Starmer’s leadership became increasingly defined by domestic policy reversals, public frustration over cost of living pressures and criticism that Labour had failed to deliver visible change despite its commanding parliamentary majority.

Several ministerial departures and internal dissatisfaction fuelled concerns the government lacked direction.

Labour also faced pressure from outside parliament, with the anti-immigration Reform UK party gaining support and reshaping political debate.

The pressure intensified following poor local and regional election results in May, prompting questions within Labour about whether Starmer remained the right person to lead the party into the next general election, expected in 2029.

While Starmer had publicly insisted he intended to continue, reports emerged that senior figures had privately urged him to step aside and allow Labour to reset before support eroded further.

In his resignation speech, Starmer said he accepted that colleagues believed a change in leadership was necessary.

Attention has quickly turned to who could become the UK's next prime minister, with former Greater Manchester mayor Andy Burnham confirming he will seek the Labour leadership.

title.en: 'Unprecedented': Is this the moment US-Israel ties stopped being 'special'?
title.zh: “前所未有”：现在是美以关系不再“特殊”的时刻吗？

summary.en: Donald Trump and his vice president's remarks about Israel have left some wondering if US-Israeli relations are irrevocably changed.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
At the White House press briefing room, the United States vice president JD Vance recently delivered a scathing rebuke to Israeli cabinet ministers critical of the United States' deal with Iran .

"Donald J Trump is the only head of state in the entire world who is sympathetic to the nation of Israel at this moment in time," he said late last week.

"If I was in the cabinet of the Israeli government, I might not be attacking the only powerful ally that I have anywhere left in the entire world."

It was, in some respects, extraordinary. US leaders have previously expressed frustration — even sworn — at Israeli officials in private. But the comments from Vance so publicly putting Israeli officials in their place were unexpected.

"Since really the Eisenhower administration [1953-1961], the United States has tended to criticise Israel behind closed doors, not in public, so this criticism in public is fairly unprecedented," Brendon O'Connor, a professor of US Politics and US Foreign Relations, told SBS News.

The comments, along with plummeting American public sentiment towards Israel and the war in Iran , have raised questions about the future of what has been dubbed as the "special relationship".

Trita Parsi, executive vice president at the Washington-based Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft, says the Trump administration is taking the first steps toward "de-specialising" the US-Israel relationship.

"What the administration is doing now is beginning to be what I would think is the contours of a deep specialisation of the US-Israeli relationship, meaning that it is a very important relationship, but it is downgraded to being at the same level as the US has with France, for instance," he told CNN.

In June, US President Donald Trump called Netanyahu "f---ing crazy" over Israel's military escalation in Lebanon. Last week, he said Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had "no f---ing judgment" after Israeli strikes targeted Beirut amid ongoing Iran war negotiations.

This may be the first time that a sitting US president has publicly attacked an Israeli prime minister, but it's not the first instance in private. Bill Clinton, for example, is said to have been incensed after a 1996 meeting with Netanyahu, reportedly telling aides: "Who the f--- does he think he is?"

More recently, then president Joe Biden is reported to have called Netanyahu a "f---ing liar" about a Gaza military decision.

title.en: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer announces resignation after months of party pressure

summary.en: The UK prime minister announced his resignation after facing months of pressure from his party, stating his commitment to ensuring a smooth transition of power.
summary.zh: 英国首相在面临数月党内压力后宣布辞职，并表示将尽力确保权力有序过渡。

body.en:
United Kingdom Prime Minister Keir Starmer says he will resign, with a new leader to be in place by the time UK parliament returns in September, paving the way for Britain to have its seventh leader in 10 years.

In an emotional speech on Monday, Starmer said he had listened to his governing Labour Party and realised he was no longer the person to lead it into a national election in 2029.

After spending weeks saying he would fight any challenge to his position as prime minister, Starmer spent the weekend reflecting on his political future at his country residence, watching his support in the party drain away.

Outside his office and London residence on Downing Street, Starmer said he would ask the Labour Party's organising committee to set out a timeline for a leadership contest to find his replacement.

Nominations would open on 9 July, close by mid-July, and if there is a contest, a new leader will be in place by September. He did not mention his rival, Andy Burnham, who is widely expected to replace him.

"The question my party is asking now is whether I am best placed to lead us into the next general election. I have heard the answer from my parliamentary party to that question and I accept that answer with good grace," he said.

After describing the achievements his government had secured in his two years of power, a man who was often criticised for being robotic, became visibly emotional, his voice cracking when he thanked his family for their support.

"When I leave the biggest job in the country, I will spend more time on the most important job, being the best husband I can to my fantastic wife, Vic, who has been a rock by my side through good times and bad, and being the best dad I can to my beautiful children, who are my pride and my joy."

Whoever replaces Starmer will become the UK's seventh prime minister since the Brexit vote to leave the European Union, which took place 10 years ago this week.

That level of turnover — the highest in the UK in nearly two centuries — underlines the struggle of maintaining the support of voters angry at successive failures to improve living standards, public services and tackle illegal immigration.

body.en:
When Donald Trump returned to the White House last year, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni was the only European leader to attend the inauguration.

Seventeen months later, their relationship is publicly breaking down, as the two right-wing leaders trade barbs on social media.

Trump's relationships with traditional European allies have further strained in his second term, and he's become increasingly unpopular among voters in much of Western Europe.

He's clashed with leaders including Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz over his decision to go to war with Iran.

And earlier this year, he shattered trust within the NATO military alliance with threats to take over Greenland.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The deterioration of the relationship with Meloni raises questions about who, if anyone, still has the US president's ear in Europe.

Meloni was viewed as one of the few leaders capable of acting as a bridge between Trump and Europe, dubbed a "Trump whisperer" by some commentators.

But cracks appeared after the US and Israel started a war with Iran earlier this year, triggering global oil price surges , damaging European economies and igniting strong anti-war sentiment in Italy.

In April, Trump lashed out at Pope Leo XIV after the pontiff denounced the war in the Middle East, criticised Trump's threat to destroy Iranian civilisation , and called on the US president to find an "off-ramp" to end the conflict.

Facing domestic pressure at the time, Meloni said Trump's comments about the pope were "unacceptable", prompting a rebuke from Trump.

Italy had also denied the use of an airbase in Sicily to US military planes carrying weapons for the war in Iran, saying the Americans had not followed the necessary procedures.

To onlookers at the G7 summit in France last week, Trump and Meloni appeared as though they might have reconciled.

That impression was short-lived. On Friday, Italian TV channel La7 quoted Trump as saying Meloni "begged me to take a picture with her".

"I wouldn't have taken it, but I felt sorry for her," Trump said, according to the broadcaster's translation.

Responding in a video on social media, Meloni said Trump's statements were fabricated.

"I am frankly astonished. I don't know why the president of the United States behaves like this towards his allies. It is not the first time," she said.

"It is disappointing that he does not show the same determination with the enemies of the West and of the United States, whose leaders he instead treats with far greater indulgence. Neither I nor Italy ever beg."

body.en:
Before being imprisoned for 20 years, Jimmy Lai founded Hong Kong's largest pro-democracy newspaper. His son said the award shows that those who fight for the freedom of others "are never alone."

Arriving in Hong Kong as a penniless 12-year-old stowaway from southern China, Jimmy Lai sought only freedom and a future. At the time, Lai could never have imagined how his life would become forever intertwined with this former British colony.

"I'll sink with the ship, because this place gives me everything," said Lai in an interview about Hong Kong with DW a few months before he was taken into custody in December 2020. He was one of the first high-profile figures to be targeted under a "national security law" imposed on Hong Kong by Beijing following a crackdown on pro-democracy protests.

Beijing had said the law would restore Hong Kong "from chaos to order" after demonstrations in 2019 opposing an extradition bill morphed into massive protests against Beijing encroaching on Hong Kong's civil liberties .

Since then, the pro-democracy media mogul has spent more than 2,000 days in solitary confinement in Hong Kong's maximum-security Stanley Prison.

Lai's years-long trial ended this February, when the 78-year-old was sentenced to 20 years in prison for "colluding with foreign forces." While he had pleaded not guilty to all charges, his legal team said he will not appeal.

The sentence is the heaviest punishment handed down so far under the national security law, and Lai's trial has symbolized for many people the severe erosion of press freedom in Hong Kong as part of Beijing's broader strategy to silence critical voices.

In recognition of his defense of press freedom and freedom of speech, DW honored Jimmy Lai with this year's Freedom of Speech Award  at the annual Global Media Forum in Bonn, Germany, on Tuesday.

"While we have spoken freely in the defence of independent media, Jimmy, who founded an independent media company because he believed in the rights of the Hong Kong people to receive information, is locked away for those beliefs," Jodie Ginsberg, CEO of the Committee to Protect Journalists, said in a speech honoring Lai.

"The attacks on Apple Daily and its counterparts in Hong Kong presaged the far greater attacks on civil liberties in the years that followed. Jimmy Lai saw this and spoke out. We can honor him today not only by fighting for his freedom, but by defending the freedoms for which he was jailed."

Since 2015, the DW Freedom of Speech Award has honored journalists and human rights defenders as a way to call attention to restrictions on press freedom and concerning human rights situations around the world.

title.en: Dettol apologises after ad to clean up 'toxic men' backfires in China
title.zh: 滴露消毒水因“清理有毒男性”广告在中国引发争议后道歉

summary.en: Dettol has issued an apology after an advertisement in China, which featured a man seeking a partner "not tainted by other men," drew widespread accusations of sexism and caused a public backlash.
summary.zh: 滴露消毒水在中国发布的一则广告引发了性别歧视的广泛指责和公众强烈反弹后，已发表道歉。该广告中一名男子寻找一位“未被其他男性玷污”的伴侣。

body.en:
British hygiene brand Dettol has apologised for an advert in China that it claims was meant to call out sexism, but has instead backfired.

The five-minute long advert for a multipurpose disinfectant, styled like a micro drama, starts out with a man looking for a partner who is "clean" and "not tainted by other men".

A plot twist comes late in the advert when his new girlfriend calls him out for his misogyny and breaks up with him. Dettol is then presented as the solution against "toxic men [who] are just like bacteria".

The advert sparked an uproar on the Chinese internet, with some users saying it objectifies women and others calling for a boycott of the brand.

Dettol said the advert, which has been removed following the backlash, was intended to criticise gender stereotypes, but that snippets of it that later circulated online distorted its core message.

"We recognise that it has offended many people, especially women. We take responsibility for any negligence in creating and reviewing the content of the advert," Dettol said in a statement on Monday.

Dettol was founded with a mission to "protect the health" of families, it said, adding: "But we are well aware that true protection also lies in safeguarding the dignity of every individual and their right to be treated equally."

The advert has sparked heated discussions across Chinese social media platforms over the last few days, with many people angered by its attempts to compare a person's "purity" with the disinfecting abilities of Dettol products.

"What a trashy advertisement. It's left me speechless," a user wrote on Weibo, China's X-like platform.

"What a hopeless company. What is their senior management doing?" read another comment. "I'm never using Dettol again. There are so many brands in the market after all."

Manya Koetse, who runs the Eye on Digital China newsletter, described the campaign as "quite a mess for a brand whose entire business revolves around cleanliness".

"Even if the intention was to portray the male character as being in the wrong, the message was conveyed so poorly that it backfired spectacularly," she said.

This is not the first time Dettol, which is owned by British consumer goods company Reckitt, has found itself at the centre of controversy in China.

It drew backlash last year with an advert that featured the line: "The woman was 'returned' just before her wedding; it must be because she was not clean."
body.zh: 英国卫生品牌滴露 (Dettol) 为在中国的一则广告道歉，该广告声称该广告旨在呼吁性别歧视，但结果适得其反。 这则长达五分钟的多用途消毒剂广告，风格像一部微剧，一开始是一个男人寻找“干净”、“没有被其他男人玷污”的伴侣。 广告后期出现了情节转折，他的新女友斥责他厌女症并与他分手。随后，滴露被提出作为对抗“有毒的人[他们]就像细菌一样”的解决方案。 该广告在中国互联网上引发轩然大波，一些用户表示该广告物化了女性，另一些用户则呼吁抵制该品牌。 戴托表示，这则广告在遭到强烈反对后已被删除，其目的是批评性别刻板印象，但后来在网上流传的广告片段歪曲了其核心信息。 “我们认识到这冒犯了很多人，尤其是女性。我们对广告内容制作和审查过程中的任何疏忽承担责任，”Dettol 在周一的一份声明中表示。 滴露成立的使命是“保护家庭健康”，并补充说：“但我们很清楚，真正的保护还在于维护每个人的尊严及其受到平等对待的权利。” 过去几天，这则广告在中国社交媒体平台上引发了热烈讨论，许多人对其试图将人的“纯洁”与滴露产品的消毒能力进行比较感到愤怒。 “真是垃圾广告，让我无语了，”一位用户在中国类似X的平台微博上写道。 “真是一个没希望的公司，他们的高层在做什么？”阅读另一条评论。 “我再也不会用滴露了，毕竟市场上品牌那么多。” 《数字中国之眼》时事通讯的负责人曼雅·科茨 (Manya Koetse) 形容这次活动“对于一个整个业务都围绕清洁展开的品牌来说相当混乱”。 “即使意图将男性角色描绘成错误的，但信息传达得非常糟糕，以至于适得其反，”她说。 英国消费品公司利洁时(Reckitt)旗下的滴露(Dettol)并不是第一次在中国成为争议的焦点。 去年，它的一则广告引起了强烈反对，其中的一句台词是：“女人在婚礼前被‘退回’；一定是因为她不干净。”

reflection.en: This incident reminds us that every person, male and female, is created in the image of Yahweh, possessing inherent dignity and worth. True respect for others means recognizing their value regardless of societal judgments or past experiences.
reflection.zh: 这一事件提醒我们，每个人，无论男女，都是照着雅伟的形象被造的，拥有固有的尊严和价值。真正尊重他人意味着无论社会评判或过往经历如何，都要承认他们的价值。

verse.textEn: So God created mankind in his own image, in the image of God he created them; male and female he created them.
verse.textZh: 神就照着自己的形象造人，乃是照着他的形象造男造女。

title.en: US-Iran deal: Pakistan's diplomatic masterstroke?
title.zh: 美伊协议：巴基斯坦的外交妙招？

summary.en: Pakistan has reportedly elevated its diplomatic standing by mediating in the Iran war, transitioning from a regional player to a global diplomatic stakeholder. This achievement was supported by China and its allies in the Gulf region.
summary.zh: 据报道，巴基斯坦通过在伊朗战争中进行调解，成功地将其地位从一个区域参与者提升为全球外交利益攸关者。这一成就得到了中国及其在海湾地区盟友的帮助。

body.en:
By stepping in as mediator in the Iran war, Pakistan has managed to elevate its status from a regional player to a global diplomatic stakeholder — with a little help from China and its friends in the Gulf.

The US-Iran deal, serving as foundation for the ongoing talks in Switzerland , marks a crucial diplomatic achievement for Pakistan, perhaps the most significant in the country's modern history. 

"Pakistan was not only able to effectively leverage its relations with Tehran and growing closeness to Washington but also its network of regional partners like Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey," Farwa Aamer, director of South Asia Initiatives at the Asia Society Policy Institute in New York, told DW.

"It gave Pakistan more diplomatic weight and international support going into the mediation role," she added.  

Islamabad also boasts close ties with China — not an easy feat on a continent increasingly shaped by the Washington-Beijing rivalry .

"Pakistan's patient diplomacy was critical in getting the US-Iran deal across the finish line, though its long-term impact will depend on the agreement's durability as difficult negotiations continue," Elizabeth Threlkeld, South Asia director at the Washington-based Stimson Center, told DW.

She lauded Islamabad for balancing ties with the US and Iran while also keeping key Gulf partners and China onboard, and "helping to find formulations that worked for all sides."

But good working relationships with regional and global powers were just a starting point. The Pakistani government has been pursuing a hands-on diplomatic strategy towards Tehran, with Pakistan's most senior military commander Asim Munir and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif both visiting Iran in May 2025, just weeks before the short-lived conflict with Israel that ended with the US bombing Iran's nuclear facilities.

"Asim Munir and Shehbaz Sharif had both traveled to Iran that summer. That is when, in my view, the Trump administration first began to recognize that the Pakistanis could be a viable and trustworthy mediator," Michael Kugelman, a senior fellow for South Asia at Washington-based Atlantic Council, told DW.

Army chief Munir, in particular, seem to have left a positive impression on Donald Trump , with the US president repeatedly praising him as a "great fighter," "an exceptional human being" and "my favorite field marshal."

The Pakistani leaders had much to lose with the US-Israel conflict with Iran spiraling into an all-out regional war. Pakistan shares a border with Iran and relies heavily on Gulf trade routes, so prolonged instability could trigger refugee flows, economic disruption, and security challenges along its western frontier. 

Once the US and Israel launched new airstrikes against Iran...
body.zh: 通过介入伊朗战争的调解人，在中国及其海湾朋友的一点帮助下，巴基斯坦成功地将其地位从地区参与者提升为全球外交利益相关者。 美国与伊朗的协议是瑞士正在进行的谈判的基础，标志着巴基斯坦的一项重要外交成就，也许是该国现代史上最重要的成就。 纽约亚洲协会政策研究所南亚倡议主任法瓦·阿梅尔 (Farwa Aamer) 告诉德国之声：“巴基斯坦不仅能够有效地利用与德黑兰的关系以及与华盛顿日益密切的关系，而且还能够有效地利用卡塔尔、沙特阿拉伯和土耳其等地区合作伙伴网络。” 她补充说：“这为巴基斯坦发挥调解作用提供了更多的外交影响力和国际支持。” 伊斯兰堡还拥有与中国的密切关系——在一个日益受到华盛顿与北京竞争影响的大陆上，这并不是一件容易的事。 华盛顿史汀生中心南亚部主任伊丽莎白·斯雷尔凯尔德 (Elizabeth Threlkeld) 向德国之声表示：“巴基斯坦的耐心外交对于美伊协议的顺利完成至关重要，但其长期影响将取决于协议的持久性，因为谈判仍在艰难进行。” 她赞扬伊斯兰堡平衡与美国和伊朗的关系，同时也让主要海湾合作伙伴和中国保持参与，并“帮助找到对各方都有效的方案”。 但与地区和全球大国的良好工作关系只是一个起点。巴基斯坦政府一直在对德黑兰采取务实的外交战略，巴基斯坦最高军事指挥官阿西姆·穆尼尔和总理谢赫巴兹·谢里夫均于 2025 年 5 月访问伊朗，而就在几周前，巴基斯坦与以色列发生了短暂的冲突，最终美国轰炸了伊朗核设施。 华盛顿大西洋理事会南亚问题高级研究员迈克尔·库格曼（Michael Kugelman）告诉德国之声：“那年夏天，阿西姆·穆尼尔和谢巴兹·谢里夫都曾前往伊朗。在我看来，特朗普政府就是在那时开始认识到巴基斯坦可以成为可行且值得信赖的调解人。” 尤其是陆军参谋长穆尼尔，似乎给唐纳德·特朗普留下了积极的印象，美国总统多次称赞他是“伟大的战士”、“杰出的人”和“我最喜欢的陆军元帅”。 随着美以与伊朗的冲突演变成全面的地区战争，巴基斯坦领导人损失惨重。巴基斯坦与伊朗接壤，严重依赖海湾贸易路线，因此长期不稳定可能会引发难民潮、经济混乱和其西部边境的安全挑战。 一旦美国和以色列对伊朗发动新的空袭……

reflection.en: This news highlights the vital role nations can play in de-escalating conflict and fostering dialogue. When a country steps forward to mediate, it embodies the spirit of peacemaking, working to bridge divides and bring stability. Such efforts reflect the blessed calling to be a peacemaker in a fractured world, for Yahweh calls those who make peace His...
reflection.zh: 这则新闻突显了国家在缓和冲突和促进对话方面可以发挥的关键作用。当一个国家挺身而出进行调解时，它体现了缔造和平的精神，努力弥合分歧并带来稳定。这样的努力反映了在一个破碎世界中成为和平缔造者的蒙福呼召，因为雅伟称那些缔造和平的人为祂的儿女。

verse.textEn: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
verse.textZh: 使人和睦的人有福了，因为他们必称为神的儿子。

title.en: ‘A hunting ground for foreign regimes’: why violent attacks on dissidents are on the rise in Britain
title.zh: “外国政权的猎场”：为何针对异议人士的暴力袭击在英国日益增多

summary.en: Reports indicate a rise in violent attacks on dissidents living in the UK, with Iran and China accused of targeting critics. An arson attack on Prime Minister Keir Starmer’s properties has also been linked to Russia.
summary.zh: 报道指出，居住在英国的异议人士遭受的暴力袭击有所增加，伊朗和中国被指控针对批评者。针对首相基尔·斯塔默房产的纵火袭击也被认为与俄罗斯有关。

body.en: Iran and China among those accused of targeting critics living in the UK, as arson attack on prime minister Keir Starmer’s properties linked to Russia As Pouria Zeraati was crossing the street between his Wimbledon home and his car in south London in March 2024, he was confronted by two men. One held him firmly as the other stabbed him three times in the leg before they both fled. It was later said to be a targeted attack on behalf of the Iranian regime in Tehran. A punishment for Zeraati’s work as a journalist covering Iran . He survived, but the ambush is one of dozens of violent incidents in recent years linked to foreign states. Russia, China, India, Saudi Arabia and Iran have all been blamed for targeting critics and dissidents living in the UK in the past decade, and linked to incidents involving physical assaults, attempted kidnap, stabbings and an acid attack. Continue reading...
body.zh: 伊朗和中国被指控针对居住在英国的批评者，对首相基尔·斯塔默与俄罗斯有关的财产进行纵火袭击。 2024 年 3 月，当普里亚·泽拉蒂 (Pouria Zeraati) 在伦敦南部温布尔登的家和他的汽车之间过马路时，遇到了两名男子。一个人牢牢地抓住了他，另一个人则在他的腿上刺了三刀，然后他们就逃跑了。后来据称这是针对德黑兰伊朗政权的一次有针对性的袭击。对泽拉蒂作为报道伊朗的记者的惩罚。他幸存下来，但这次伏击是近年来与外国有关的数十起暴力事件之一。俄罗斯、中国、印度、沙特阿拉伯和伊朗都被指责在过去十年中针对居住在英国的批评者和持不同政见者，并与涉及人身攻击、企图绑架、刺伤和硫酸袭击的事件有关。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This report highlights the chilling reality of oppressive regimes extending their reach to silence critics abroad. Proverbs 28:15 reminds us that a wicked ruler can be like a dangerous predator to a helpless people, illustrating the vulnerability of those who speak truth to power. In such times, we pray for the safety of dissidents and for justice to...
reflection.zh: 这篇报道揭示了压迫性政权将魔爪伸向海外，以压制批评者的严峻现实。箴言28:15提醒我们，邪恶的统治者对无助的人民来说，如同咆哮的狮子或冲锋的熊，这形象地描绘了那些向权力说真话的人所面临的脆弱处境。在这样的时刻，我们为异议人士的安全祷告，并祈求公义战胜那些试图压制自由的势力。

verse.textEn: Like a roaring lion or a charging bear is a wicked ruler over a helpless people.
verse.textZh: 暴虐的君王辖制贫民，好像吼叫的狮子、觅食的熊。

title.en: Petrol prices in Australia are now lower than before the Iran war began. Is the oil crisis over and what happens next?
title.zh: 澳大利亚汽油价格已低于伊朗战争爆发前水平。石油危机结束了吗？接下来会发生什么？

summary.en: Australian petrol prices have fallen below pre-Middle East conflict levels, surprising analysts who had warned of shortages and record high prices. This unexpected flexibility from non-Middle Eastern fuel suppliers, including China, has led to a significant drop in costs.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚的汽油价格已降至中东冲突爆发前的水平，这出乎分析师的意料，他们此前曾警告可能出现燃料短缺和价格飙升。中东以外的燃料供应商，包括中国，展现出超出预期的灵活性，导致油价显著下降。

body.en: Fuel suppliers outside the Middle East have proved to be much more flexible than analysts expected – and China surprised everyone Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Australians were warned soon after the Middle East conflict started that the country could run short on fuel, with prices rising to record levels owing to disrupted oil supplies. Now, amid an uneasy peace deal and continued supply disruptions, petrol prices are lower than they were before the conflict began and official warnings over fuel usage have largely disappeared. Continue reading...
body.zh: 事实证明，中东以外的燃料供应商比分析师预期的灵活得多，而中国令所有人感到惊讶。中东冲突爆发后不久，澳大利亚人就收到警告称，该国可能出现燃料短缺，由于石油供应中断，价格上涨至创纪录水平。现在，由于和平协议不稳定，供应持续中断，汽油价格低于冲突开始前，官方对燃料使用的警告也基本消失。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The unexpected drop in petrol prices, after initial warnings of scarcity and record highs, reminds us that periods of anxiety can give way to relief. Just as weeping may endure for a night, joy can indeed come in the morning, often through unforeseen circumstances. This turn of events offers a hopeful perspective on how challenges can resolve in ways we...
reflection.zh: 汽油价格在最初警告可能出现短缺和创纪录高位后，意外下降，这提醒我们，焦虑时期可能会迎来缓解。正如哭泣可能持续一夜，喜乐确实会在早晨到来，而且常常是通过意想不到的情况。这一转变提供了一个充满希望的视角，说明挑战可能以我们未曾预料的方式得到解决。

verse.textEn: Weeping may stay for the night, but rejoicing comes in the morning.
verse.textZh: 一宿虽然有哭泣，早晨便必欢呼。

title.en: Charging ahead: EVs outpace growth predictions
title.zh: 电动汽车：超越增长预期，加速前进

summary.en: Electric vehicles are becoming more affordable, efficient, and capable of longer distances, exceeding initial growth forecasts. China is leading this transition, with Europe and other nations rapidly advancing as well.
summary.zh: 电动汽车正变得更便宜、更高效，续航里程也比以往任何时候都长，其增长速度超出了预期。中国正在推动这一转型，而欧洲和其他国家也正在迅速追赶。

body.zh: 电动汽车变得越来越便宜、越来越高效，而且行驶距离比以往任何时候都更远。中国正在推动这一转型，但欧洲和其他国家正在快速追赶。 全球电动汽车 (EV) 市场的增长速度远远快于预期。短短六年内，销量增长了十倍，到 2025 年，全球电动汽车销量将达到约 2100 万辆。 中国和欧洲处于领先地位，但世界其他地区的市场也在快速增长。 中国长期以来一直在投资太阳能和风能以及电池技术——电动汽车最关键的组成部分。 得益于先进的研究和大规模生产，电动汽车电池成本大幅下降。如今，它们的成本仅为 10 年前的四分之一，而且价格还在继续下降。 中国是世界上最大的汽车市场，消费者正在从政府的产业战略中获益。自 2024 年以来，电动汽车的成本低于内燃机汽车，国家多年来一直在迅速扩大充电基础设施，而且中国的电力非常实惠。 2015年，电动汽车仅占中国新车销量的1%。到 2026 年 4 月，这一比例已攀升至 61%。 电动汽车依靠电力运行并通过电缆充电。在全球范围内，三分之二的电动汽车是所谓的电池电动汽车 (BEV)，仅由电力驱动。剩下的三分之一还配备了燃气发动机，用于长途旅行时的备用——这些被称为增程电动汽车 (EREV) 或插电式混合动力电动汽车 (PHEV)。 相比之下，所谓的混合动力电动汽车 (HEV) 始终需要汽油或柴油来为其内燃机提供动力。电动机提供一些帮助，仅通过再生制动产生电力。这项技术在一定程度上降低了城市驾驶的燃油消耗，但混合动力汽车在国际统计中并未被算作电动汽车。 2018年，电动汽车仅占欧盟新车注册量的1%。到 2026 年 4 月，售出的新车中近三分之一是电动汽车。 北欧处于领先地位。在挪威，现在销售的几乎所有新车都是电动汽车（99%），其次是丹麦（82%）和瑞典（65%）。该地区各国政府支持气候友好型出行，并正在扩大充电基础设施。 在英国，2026 年 4 月注册的新车中有 39% 是电动汽车，其次是德国（37%）和法国（32%）。在这三个国家，电动汽车销量与去年同月相比都翻了一番。 近年来，美国市场陷入停滞。 2023 年至 2025 年间，电动汽车占...

reflection.en: The rapid advancements in electric vehicle technology, making them cheaper and more efficient, reflect a remarkable acceleration of human knowledge and innovation. This progress reminds us of the human capacity to explore and develop new solutions, continually expanding our understanding and capabilities.
reflection.zh: 电动汽车技术日新月异，变得更便宜、更高效，这反映了人类知识和创新的显著加速。这种进步提醒我们，人类有能力探索和开发新的解决方案，不断拓展我们的理解和能力。

verse.textEn: But you, Daniel, roll up and seal the words of the scroll until the time of the end. Many will go here and there to increase knowledge.
verse.textZh: 但以理啊，你要隐藏这话，封闭这书，直到末时。必有多人来往奔跑，知识就必增长。

title.en: For women in China frustrated by sexism, female comics are offering a release
title.zh: 在中国，女性喜剧演员为厌倦性别歧视的女性提供宣泄出口

summary.en: Standup comedy in China is providing a platform for women to discuss sensitive topics, including sexism, offering a sense of release and shared experience. Performers, however, remain cautious of censorship limits as they navigate this space in venues like a small performing arts theatre in east Beijing.
summary.zh: 中国的脱口秀喜剧为女性提供了一个平台，让她们可以讨论包括性别歧视在内的敏感话题，从而获得宣泄和共同的体验。然而，表演者们在北京东部一家小型表演艺术剧院等场所进行表演时，仍对审查限制保持警惕。

body.en: Standup comedy gives women a space to talk about certain topics that have become more sensitive, while performers remain wary of censorship limits Packed into the upstairs theatre of a small performing arts space in east Beijing, more than 100 people, mostly women, are giddy with anticipation. “Who did you come to see?” asks the MC, fashionably dressed in a faded denim two-piece suit. The answer is bellowed in unison back to him: “Fang Zhuren!” Fang Shaoli, AKA Director Fang ( Fang Zhuren ), has built a cult following in China in the past two years. Decidedly less fashionable than the evening’s host, Fang is dressed in a yellow hoodie and dark blue jeans. Her everywoman attire is part of the appeal. With a stout frame and short, sensible haircut, Fang, who was born in 1975, hails from rural part of east China’s Shandong province. Before discovering the art of standup comedy she worked in factories and on construction sites, but mainly lived as a housewife to a difficult husband. Her jokes riff on the deep sexism that permeates Chinese culture, particularly away from the big urban centres like Beijing and Shanghai. Continue reading...

summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
For much of the past century, Labor has promised to end Australia's status as the only developed democracy without a national human rights act.

After several abandoned and botched attempts by previous governments, the landmark reform is again in the in-tray.

A government-tasked parliamentary committee report is the latest to recommend change and Hobart-based MP Andrew Wilkie has introduced a private member's bill to legislate it.

The Coalition is firmly opposed but the Greens have signalled support, meaning Labor has the numbers to pass the law.

However, Anthony Albanese's government is proceeding with caution, with Attorney-General Michelle Rowland saying for two years it is "carefully considering" the complex policy area.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

History — and a hard-nosed read of the political environment — suggests Labor is unlikely to enact a human rights act, even as advocates contend the time is right.

"We have royal commissions indicating what happens when human rights standards are not in federal law," Daney Faddoul, campaign manager at the Human Rights Law Centre, told the Australian Associated Press (AAP) news agency.

He is referring to the 2018 aged care and 2019 disability probes, which found mass breaches of human rights and a need to legislate protections to prevent future abuse.

Also the subject of a 2022 royal commission, the infamous Robodebt scandal is another product of a public service which doesn't centre the rights of its citizens.

"Our constitution has very few human rights protections in it," Australian Human Rights Commission president Hugh de Kretser says.

"In every other comparable democracy that's been done either through constitutional protection or through a human rights act."

Both the commission and law centre are part of a huge civil push for a federal act.

More than 175 organisations, including peak bodies, religious groups, legal bodies, unions, disability advocates, service providers, and ethnic communities have signed up.

At its heart, the reform is very simple: to codify into a single law the rights Australia has already agreed to protect in international treaties.

Questions like what rights to include, how strictly they should be enforced and whether courts can strike down inconsistent laws.

title.en: Robodebt victims share in millions as Australia's largest-ever class action settlement approved

summary.en: The bungled Robodebt program has cost the government more than $2.4 billion following multiple class action lawsuits.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Australia's biggest class action settlement in history will be paid out to victims of the government's robodebt scheme after a lengthy court approval process.

About 125,000 registered claimants who were affected by the federal government's unlawful debt collection method will receive $475 million in compensation between them.

The Robodebt system was designed to fix overpayment of social security benefits, but it resulted in hundreds of thousands of people being wrongly accused of owing the government money between 2015 and 2019.

Some of Australia's most vulnerable people entered into extreme debt, went without food or even died by suicide as a result.

The bungled program has cost the government more than $2.4 billion following multiple class actions.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Federal Court Justice Jonathan Beach ruled on Tuesday that an additional settlement of $548.5 million, including the approved compensation figure, was fair and reasonable.

It also includes up to $13.5 million in legal costs, to be paid by the Commonwealth.

Class action representatives will be paid between $20,000 and $25,000 each for "inconvenience occurred over a number of years".

The settlement comes on top of an earlier $112 million agreement that lawyers successfully appealed.

Justice Beach thanked victims who had been part of various class actions since 2019, particularly Jenny Miller and Kath Madgwick.

They lost their sons, Rhys Cauzzo and Jarrad Madgwick, to suicide after they were issued with robodebt notices.

"I did appreciate hearing their perspectives and the fortitude that has been shown particularly from the two mothers whose sons were lost," the judge said.

He added the "fiasco" was an opportunity to learn lessons, chastising government officials who were 'insulated and detached" from the consequences of their actions.

A settlement was first reached in 2021, but it did not consider information later uncovered in the Royal Commission into the Robodebt Scheme.

That included the revelation that government officials tried to mislead investigations into the scandal.

Further compensation was then requested in the successful appeal by law firm Gordon Legal, which led the class action.

The class action was launched by Sydney woman Katherine Prygodicz, who had twice been chased for a debt of more than $14,000.

Despite having his bail varied to attend the event in Canberra on Tuesday evening, Sydney's Downing Centre Local Court was told the former special forces soldier did not end up travelling to the ACT.

"Mr Roberts-Smith felt ill in the last couple days and hasn't travelled to Canberra today to attend the official opening at the war memorial," defence lawyer Slade Howell said.

The Victoria Cross recipient, who faces five counts of war crime murder , was going to attend the official opening of Anzac Hall and the memorial's atrium, displaying Australia's commitments to the Middle East, Afghanistan and peacekeeping operations.

"The Victoria Cross recipients have been invited to this, which is appropriate. I'm comfortable about that," he told ABC TV on Tuesday.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and One Nation Leader Pauline Hanson will be among those at the opening.

Hanson had said she was hoping to speak with Roberts-Smith during the event and that he was welcome to attend given he wasn't yet convicted of a crime .

body.en:
After years without a single case, H5 bird flu was detected in Australia for the first time last week. The virus has had devastating consequences on wildlife and poultry on other continents. What could happen now that it's finally reached our shores?

A brown skua and a northern giant petrel in Western Australia have tested positive for the H5N1 strain of the virus, prompting precautionary lockdowns at some WA poultry production facilities.

Both animals were discovered on a remote beach in Esperance, about 700km south-east of Perth.

While spread to humans is rare, the virus can infect or cause illness in a range of animal species, including dairy cattle, domestic cats, pigs, goats, horses and seals. In chickens, an infection is typically fatal.

There's no evidence to suggest the strain has been found in local poultry or agriculture, federal Agriculture Minister Julie Collins said.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

The federal government has reiterated that Australia is well-prepared for the arrival of the virus, which has been circulating globally since 2020.

Authorities are still investigating whether the virus is widespread in Australian wildlife or contained to a few isolated cases in migratory birds.

But Collins warned lessons from overseas indicated the virus cannot be prevented from spreading, and Australia can't stop it from arriving via migratory birds.

"Experts will decide whether or not it's eradicable or whether or not we manage the disease," she said.

During previous avian influenza outbreaks, egg and poultry production were impacted in some parts of Australia, causing the cost of eggs to spike and shortages to occur.

In 2024 and 2025, egg shortages were reported in Australia after hundreds of thousands of hens were euthanised to contain the spread of the highly pathogenic virus.

More than 200 million chickens have been culled in the US since the virus arrived there.

Robyn Alders is a veterinary immunology expert and honorary professor at the Australian National University's Development Policy Centre.

She said the characteristics of the H5N1 bird flu variant are "significantly different from the bird flu viruses that Australia has dealt with in the past".

"We know what happened to egg prices during the last outbreak, and that was an H7 — so, a different strain of bird flu — but one that behaves like the old bird flus that we knew," she told SBS News.

She also noted that heightened biosecurity measures, such as bringing free range hens into indoor housing to prevent exposure to wild birds, can also come at a cost to producers, which could be passed on to consumers.
